title: Tulsidas begins a work he feels too small for
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 8 to 13 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Before the story has even begun, the poet stops and admits what he is afraid of. He wants to sing of Ram, and he believes he has neither the learning nor the skill. He expects good people to be kind and the others to laugh.
dilemma: Stay silent because the work will be imperfect, or begin anyway.
what_they_did: He says plainly that his fortune is small and his wish is large, lists his limits without drama, and begins all the same.
the_turn: He stops measuring the poem by his own skill and rests it on its subject: even a plain verse is worth hearing if it carries Ram's name. He says he has shown strength to his own mind this way, and starts.
outcome: The Manas gets written. The fear of mockery is named and then left standing where it is.
whole_arc_note: His humility is not a refusal to act. Do not clip it to self-deprecation; the passage ends in a decision to write.
teaching: A small capacity joined to a great purpose is reason enough to begin.
framework: Name the fear of being laughed at. State your limits truthfully. Find what in the work is worth more than your skill. Begin, and let the critics be.
modern_parallels: I want to start writing but everyone in this field is better than me.
I keep rewriting the first page because I am scared people will laugh.
I have a big idea and a very ordinary CV.
Who am I to make something on this subject?

key_verses.sanskrit: भाग छोट अभिलाषु बड़ करउँ एक बिस्वास। पैहहिं सुख सुनि सुजन सब खल करिहहिं उपहास ॥
key_verses.gist: My fortune is small and my wish is large; I hold one trust, that the good will be glad to hear this and the others will mock.

key_verses.sanskrit: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥
key_verses.gist: Who does not love his own verse, sweet or flat? Those who delight in another's are rare.

key_verses.sanskrit: एहि प्रकार बल मनहि देखाई। करिहउँ रघुपति कथा सुहाई॥ ब्यास आदि कबि पुंगव नाना। जिन्ह सादर हरि सुजस बखाना ॥
key_verses.gist: Having shown strength to my own mind this way, I will tell the story of Raghupati.

content_hook: The most loved book in North India opens with its author saying he is not good enough to write it.

title: Tulsidas salutes his critics before they have spoken
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 4 to 9 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: He knows the kind of person who is pained by another's gain and pleased by another's ruin, who turns against you for no reason. He knows they will come for his poem. He bows to them first, sincerely.
what_they_did: He offers a formal salutation to the ill-willed alongside the saints, describes them exactly, and then says their laughter will only do him good.
the_turn: He decides in advance that mockery cannot harm the work: crows will always call the cuckoo harsh. The critic is given a place in the opening prayers and thereby loses the power to surprise him.
outcome: He proceeds without bitterness and without waiting for approval.
whole_arc_note: The salutation is ironic and sincere at once. It does not say critics are right, and it does not say they should be fought. He sees them clearly and keeps walking.
teaching: Expect the fault-finder, greet him, and do not let him set your course.
modern_parallels: One colleague tears down everything I present, for no reason I can find.
I am afraid to post my work because of the comments.
A relative is happier at my setbacks than my wins.
I take criticism very personally even when I know it is unfair.

key_verses.sanskrit: बहुरि बंदि खल गन सतिभाएँ। जे बिनु काज दाहिनेहु बाएँ॥ पर हित हानि लाभ जिन्ह केरें। उजरें हरष बिषाद बसेरें ॥
key_verses.gist: Then I bow in good faith to the ill-willed, who turn against even their well-wishers without cause, whose gain is another's loss.

key_verses.sanskrit: खल परिहास होइ हित मोरा। काक कहहिं कलकंठ कठोरा॥ हंसहि बक दादुर चातकही। हँसहिं मलिन खल बिमल बतकही ॥
key_verses.gist: The mockery of such people will be to my good; crows call the sweet-voiced cuckoo harsh.

content_hook: Tulsidas put his critics in the opening prayers.

title: Sati doubts, tests in secret, and hides it from Shiva
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 44 to 52 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Sati sees her husband bow to a prince who is weeping through the forest for a lost wife. She cannot fit the two together: the all-pervading, unborn one, and this grieving man. Shiva explains, and the explanation does not reach her.
dilemma: Trust the word of the one she trusts most, or check for herself behind his back.
what_they_did: She goes to test Ram disguised as Sita. He greets her by name and asks where Shiva is. Walking back she sees Ram, Sita and Lakshman wherever she looks. Frightened, she tells Shiva she tested nothing.
the_turn: Shiva, letting her go, says only: what Ram has arranged will be; who can stretch the argument further. The doubt itself was open to answer. What it turns on is the concealment: out of fear she hid it from Shiva.
outcome: Shiva sees in meditation what she did. The lie, more than the doubt, is what stands between them afterwards.
whole_arc_note: The text does not punish questioning: Parvati later asks the same question openly and receives the whole Manas as the answer. What costs Sati is testing in disguise and then lying about it. Keep both halves.
teaching: A doubt brought into the open can be answered; a doubt acted on in secret and then denied breaks trust.
modern_parallels: I checked my partner's phone and then said I had not.
I could not take my mentor's word for it, so I went behind their back to verify.
My faith does not survive what I see with my own eyes, and I am ashamed to say so.
I told a small lie to cover a moment of distrust and now it sits between us.

key_verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्म जो ब्यापक बिरज अज अकल अनीह अभेद। सो कि देह धरि होइ नर जाहि न जानत बेद ॥
key_verses.gist: The Absolute, all-pervading, unborn, without parts or desire, whom even the Veda does not know: can that take a body and be a man?

key_verses.sanskrit: होइहि सोइ जो राम रचि राखा। को करि तर्क बढ़ावै साखा॥ अस कहि लगे जपन हरिनामा। गईं सती जहँ प्रभु सुखधामा ॥
key_verses.gist: What Ram has arranged, that will be; who would spin the argument out further?

key_verses.sanskrit: सतीं समुझि रघुबीर प्रभाऊ। भय बस सिव सन कीन्ह दुराऊ॥ कछु न परीछा लीन्हि गोसाईं। कीन्ह प्रनामु तुम्हारिहि नाईं ॥
key_verses.gist: Understanding Ram's greatness, out of fear she hid it from Shiva: I made no test, I only bowed as you did.

content_hook: The doubt did not end the marriage. The lie about the doubt did.
notes: gender_sensitive: the scene can be misread as a wife punished for thinking. The text has the same question honoured when Parvati asks it openly.

title: Sati lives beside a husband who has silently withdrawn
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 53 to 56 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Shiva resolves inwardly that in this body he will not be with Sati as a wife, because she took the form of Sita. He says nothing of it aloud. She senses it, cannot ask, and carries the knowledge of her own act day after day.
dilemma: She cannot confess what she denied, and cannot bear the distance it has made.
what_they_did: She grieves in silence, noting that Shiva in his depth never once named her fault. When the weight becomes unbearable she turns in her mind to Ram, the one she had doubted.
the_turn: She prays to the very one she offended: if you are called kind to the afflicted, let this body end soon. Her appeal is made in the heart, with no words she can say to anyone.
outcome: Shiva enters a long samadhi. The silence holds until Daksha's sacrifice. Her prayer is answered in her next birth as Parvati, when the question is asked openly and answered.
whole_arc_note: Her wish to leave the body belongs to her story and its rebirth; it is not counsel. The usable part is the cost of an unspoken breach and the turn toward the one wronged. Shiva's restraint in not shaming her is also part of the picture.
teaching: Guilt that cannot be spoken to the person hardens into distance; the text turns it toward prayer.
modern_parallels: We live in the same house and have not really spoken in months.
I know what I did, he knows I know, and neither of us says it.
My partner has gone quiet and polite and I can feel the door has closed.
I cannot confess and I cannot stop thinking about it.

key_verses.sanskrit: तब संकर प्रभु पद सिरु नावा। सुमिरत रामु हृदयँ अस आवा॥ एहिं तन सतिहि भेंट मोहि नाहीं। सिव संकल्पु कीन्ह मन माहीं ॥
key_verses.gist: Remembering Ram, this came to Shiva's heart: in this body I shall not meet Sati; and he made the resolve within.

key_verses.sanskrit: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
key_verses.gist: Thinking over what she had done, her worry had no measure: Shiva, an ocean of grace and very deep, never said my fault aloud.

key_verses.sanskrit: कहि न जाइ कछु हृदय गलानी। मन महुँ रामहि सुमिर सयानी॥ जौं प्रभु दीनदयालु कहावा। आरति हरन बेद जसु गावा ॥
key_verses.gist: The shame in her heart could not be told; wisely she remembered Ram within.

content_hook: He never said a word about it. That was the hardest part.
notes: self_harm_theme because Sati prays for her body to end. Never serve where risk is present.

title: Sati goes to her father's house where her husband is not welcome
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 56 to 61 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Her father holds a great sacrifice and invites everyone except her husband. She longs to go home anyway. Shiva tells her gently that one may visit a parent uninvited, but where someone bears a grudge, going brings no good.
dilemma: Loyalty to the family she was born into, against the dignity of the family she has made.
what_they_did: She goes. Only her mother greets her warmly. Her father does not ask after her, and there is no share set out for Shiva. She speaks out before the assembly and gives up her body in the fire of yoga.
the_turn: Shiva's counsel is the hinge: affection gives the right to arrive unasked at the house of a friend, master, father or teacher, but where there is hostility, going does not end well.
outcome: The sacrifice is destroyed. Sati is reborn as Parvati and wins Shiva again.
whole_arc_note: This is not a lesson in obeying a husband; Shiva lets her go with attendants. The point is his reading of the situation: a home that insults your partner has not invited you either. Her death must never be offered as an example.
teaching: Where a grudge is held against the one you love, your own welcome is also withdrawn, whatever the blood tie.
modern_parallels: My parents will not accept my husband and still expect me at every function.
I went to the family wedding alone and came back humiliated.
My family insults my partner and tells me not to take it personally.
I keep hoping this visit will be different.

key_verses.sanskrit: जदपि मित्र प्रभु पितु गुर गेहा। जाइअ बिनु बोलेहुँ न सँदेहा॥ तदपि बिरोध मान जहँ कोई। तहाँ गएँ कल्यानु न होई ॥
key_verses.gist: To the house of a friend, a master, a father or a teacher one may go unasked; yet where someone holds enmity, going brings no good.

key_verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मसभाँ हम सन दुखु माना। तेहि तें अजहुँ करहिं अपमाना॥ जौं बिनु बोलें जाहु भवानी। रहइ न सीलु सनेहु न कानी ॥
key_verses.gist: If you go unbidden, neither courtesy nor affection nor honour will remain.

content_hook: Her father invited the whole world and left out one name: her husband's.
notes: self_harm_theme: Sati ends her life in yogic fire. Serve only the counsel scene to at-risk readers, or not at all.

title: Shiva, bereaved, wanders and finds rest in hearing the story
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 71 to 73 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher); with Shiva's own account at Uttar Kand doha 56
the_moment: After Sati gives up her body, Shiva has no taste for anything. He tells Parvati later that he was very sorrowful in her absence and roamed mountains, forests and lakes as one detached, looking and not caring.
what_they_did: He keeps repeating Ram's name and goes wherever Ram's qualities are being sung. On the far side of Sumeru he finds the crow Bhushundi telling the story, takes the form of a swan, and stays to listen for a while.
the_turn: He does not argue himself out of grief. He gives it somewhere to sit: the name on the tongue and the company of people telling the story.
outcome: His mind steadies. Ram later appears and asks him to accept Parvati, and he agrees.
whole_arc_note: Even Shiva grieves, and the text lets him wander first. Do not shorten it to chant and move on. Listening comes after a long season of roaming.
teaching: Grief is not reasoned away; it is carried into remembrance and good company until it loosens.
modern_parallels: Since my wife died nothing interests me; I just walk.
I travel and look at beautiful places and feel nothing.
The only hour I feel settled is at the evening katha.
I do not want advice. I want somewhere to sit with this.

key_verses.sanskrit: जब तें सतीं जाइ तनु त्यागा। तब तें सिव मन भयउ बिरागा॥ जपहिं सदा रघुनायक नामा। जहँ तहँ सुनहिं राम गुन ग्रामा ॥
key_verses.gist: From the time Sati gave up her body, dispassion came over Shiva's mind; he repeated Ram's name always and listened wherever Ram's virtues were sung.

key_verses.sanskrit: तब अति सोच भयउ मन मोरें। दुखी भयउँ बियोग प्रिय तोरें॥ सुंदर बन गिरि सरित तड़ागा। कौतुक देखत फिरउँ बेरागा ॥
key_verses.gist: Then great sorrow came upon my mind; I was grieved at parting from you, dear one. I wandered among fair forests, hills, rivers and lakes, looking on as one detached.

content_hook: Even Shiva, after his wife died, just walked for a long time.

title: Parvati is told by seven sages that she has chosen badly
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 74 to 78 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: She has given years to her tapasya for Shiva on Narad's word. Seven revered sages arrive and take her choice apart: Narad ruins homes, Shiva is a homeless ascetic with snakes and ashes, and Vishnu is available and faultless.
dilemma: Respected elders offer a safer, better-looking option and call her adviser a fraud.
what_they_did: She listens, laughs, and answers each point. She grants that Shiva may be a house of faults and Vishnu the home of every virtue, and says the heart that delights in someone wants only that one.
the_turn: She says she will not drop Narad's teaching whether her house stands or falls, and that her resolve will hold through ten million births: Shiva or no one. She adds that she would not leave it even if Shiva himself said so a hundred times.
outcome: The sages, who came to test her, bow and bless her. The marriage follows.
whole_arc_note: The sages are testing, not sincere; her firmness is honoured, not corrected. This is steadiness in a considered vow made on a teacher's word, and the text does not present it as a licence for every stubbornness.
teaching: One who has no trust in the teacher's word finds neither ease nor success, even in dreams.
modern_parallels: Everyone says I am making a mistake marrying him.
My family lists why my chosen career is foolish and what the sensible option is.
People I respect are telling me my mentor misled me.
I have put years into this path and the comparison with the safe one never stops.

key_verses.sanskrit: नारद बचन न मैं परिहरऊँ। बसउ भवनु उजरउ नहिं डरउँ॥ गुर कें बचन प्रतीति न जेही। सपनेहुँ सुगम न सुख सिधि तेही ॥
key_verses.gist: I will not give up Narad's word; let my house stand or fall, I am not afraid. One without trust in the guru's word finds no ease or success even in a dream.

key_verses.sanskrit: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥
key_verses.gist: Mahadev a house of faults, Vishnu the home of all virtues; yet the heart cares only for the one it delights in.

key_verses.sanskrit: जन्म कोटि लगि रगर हमारी। बरउँ संभु न त रहउँ कुआरी॥ तजउँ न नारद कर उपदेसू। आपु कहहिं सत बार महेसू ॥
key_verses.gist: For ten million births this is my stand: I marry Shambhu or stay unwed.

content_hook: Seven sages came to tell her she had picked the wrong man. She laughed.

title: Kamadeva accepts a task he knows will destroy him
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 79 to 83 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The gods need Shiva roused from samadhi and ask Kama to do it. Kama thinks it through and sees no good ending for himself in opposing Shiva. His wife Rati will be the one left to weep.
dilemma: Refuse and keep his life, or do the work others need and lose it.
what_they_did: He says that all the same he will do their work, for scripture calls helping others the highest dharma. He goes, is burned by Shiva's third eye, and Rati comes weeping to Shiva.
the_turn: His own line: one who gives up the body for another's good is praised by the saints for ever. And then Shiva's grace to Rati: your husband will be called the Bodiless and will pervade all, and you will meet him again.
outcome: Kama lives on without a body. Rati receives a promise of reunion. The gods' purpose is served.
whole_arc_note: Include Rati. The text does not leave the cost of his sacrifice unacknowledged, and the god who burned him is the one who consoles her.
teaching: Helping others is the highest dharma, and the text takes care to honour who pays for it.
modern_parallels: I am the one who has to take the fall for the team on this.
I volunteered for the posting nobody wanted and my family is paying the price.
My husband died doing his duty and people call it noble. I am the one left.
The right thing here will cost me the job.

key_verses.sanskrit: तदपि करब मैं काजु तुम्हारा। श्रुति कह परम धरम उपकारा॥ पर हित लागि तजइ जो देही। संतत संत प्रसंसहिं तेही ॥
key_verses.gist: Even so I will do your work; scripture calls service to others the highest dharma. One who gives up the body for another's good is praised by the saints for ever.

key_verses.sanskrit: अब तें रति तव नाथ कर होइहि नामु अनंगु। बिनु बपु ब्यापिहि सबहि पुनि सुनु निज मिलन प्रसंगु ॥
key_verses.gist: From now, Rati, your lord's name will be the Bodiless; without a body he will pervade all. Hear now how you will meet him again.

content_hook: He knew exactly how it would end for him. He went anyway.

title: Maina sees the man her daughter has chosen and breaks down
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 86 to 97 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The wedding party arrives: ghosts, ash, snakes, a bull. The women come out with the welcome lamp, see the groom and run. Maina takes her daughter in her lap and weeps that she would rather jump from a mountain with her than give her to this man.
dilemma: Protect her child from a match that looks like ruin, or honour the choice her daughter made.
what_they_did: She curses Narad for wrecking a settled home, says the world may mock but the wedding will not happen while she lives, and laments how little say a woman has in her own life.
the_turn: Parvati speaks first, calmly: do not blame anyone, what is written for me I will meet wherever I go. Then Narad and the sages tell Maina who her daughter is and who Shiva is. Seeing the hour, she takes hold of herself.
outcome: The fear turns to joy and the wedding is celebrated.
whole_arc_note: Maina's fear is love and is not mocked. Her line about women's dependence is a mother's cry at parting. It is her lament, and the scripture does not offer it as a rule. The turn comes from knowing more about the groom; she is not simply told to be quiet.
teaching: Appearance frightens love; knowledge of who the person is settles it.
modern_parallels: My daughter wants to marry someone I cannot picture in our family.
He has no proper job, no proper home, and she is certain.
I said terrible things when she told us and I do not know how to take them back.
I am terrified my child is choosing a hard life.

key_verses.sanskrit: कस कीन्ह बरु बौराह बिधि जेहिं तुम्हहि सुंदरता दई। जो फलु चहिअ सुरतरुहिं सो बरबस बबूरहिं लागई॥ तुम्ह सहित गिरि तें गिरौं पावक जरौं जलनिधि महुँ परौं। घरु जाउ अपजसु होउ जग जीवत बिबाहु न हौं करौं॥
key_verses.gist: What crazed fate gave you such beauty and such a groom? I will leap from the mountain with you, burn or drown; let home be lost and the world mock, while I live I will not make this marriage.

key_verses.sanskrit: कत बिधि सृजीं नारि जग माहीं। पराधीन सपनेहूँ सुखु नाहीं॥ भै अति प्रेम बिकल महतारी। धीरजु कीन्ह कुसमय बिचारी ॥
key_verses.gist: Why did fate make woman in this world, dependent and without happiness even in dreams? The mother, distraught with love, saw the hour was wrong and took hold of herself.

content_hook: The groom arrived with ghosts for groomsmen, and the bride's mother fainted.

title: Parvati asks the question that once cost her everything
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 100 to 113 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: In her last life this very doubt ended in disaster. Now, seated beside Shiva at ease, she still does not understand how the formless can be Dasharath's son. She could let it lie. She asks.
dilemma: Stay quiet and safe, or risk the same question again.
what_they_did: She waits for a good moment, says she is his own, admits the confusion remains, and asks him not to be angry at her ignorance but to remove it however he can.
the_turn: Shiva is delighted. He tells her she loves Ram and has asked for the good of the world, and the whole Ramcharitmanas pours out as his answer.
outcome: The doubt that was punished when hidden becomes, when voiced, the occasion for the story itself.
whole_arc_note: Read with Sati's story. Same person, same question, opposite method. The text praises the asking.
teaching: Ask plainly and at the right time; an honest question is a gift to everyone who hears the answer.
modern_parallels: I am afraid to raise the topic again because last time it went so badly.
I have a basic question about my faith and feel stupid asking.
I want to ask my manager why, without it sounding like a challenge.
There is something I never understood about my partner's beliefs.

key_verses.sanskrit: जौं मो पर प्रसन्न सुखरासी। जानिअ सत्य मोहि निज दासी॥ तौ प्रभु हरहु मोर अग्याना। कहि रघुनाथ कथा बिधि नाना ॥
key_verses.gist: If you are pleased with me and truly count me your own, then, lord, take away my ignorance and tell me Ram's story.

key_verses.sanskrit: जौं अनीह ब्यापक बिभु कोऊ। कहहु बुझाइ नाथ मोहि सोऊ॥ अग्य जानि रिस उर जनि धरहू। जेहि बिधि मोह मिटै सोइ करहू ॥
key_verses.gist: Knowing me ignorant, hold no anger in your heart; do whatever will end my confusion.

key_verses.sanskrit: पूँछेहु रघुपति कथा प्रसंगा। सकल लोक जग पावनि गंगा॥ तुम्ह रघुबीर चरन अनुरागी। कीन्हिहु प्रस्न जगत हित लागी ॥
key_verses.gist: You love the feet of Ram, and you have asked for the good of the world.

content_hook: She had already lost one life to this question. She asked it again, out loud this time.

title: Narad conquers desire, grows proud of it, and is undone by desire
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 121 to 134 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Narad sits in samadhi and Kama's whole army fails to move him. He comes out pleased with himself and tells Shiva. Shiva begs him again and again not to repeat this to Vishnu. Narad goes straight to Vishnu and tells it, with pride.
what_they_did: Passing through a city conjured by Vishnu's maya, he sees a princess choosing her husband and wants her at once. He asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu promises only what is truly good for him and gives him a monkey's. He is laughed at, loses her, and curses Vishnu in fury.
the_turn: Vishnu sees a great tree of pride sprouting in his devotee's heart and resolves to pull it up quickly, as a doctor refuses a patient the food he craves. When the maya lifts, Narad falls at his feet and asks how his harsh words can be undone. He is told to repeat Shiva's name and find rest.
outcome: The curse stands and becomes one cause of Ram's birth as a man who will be parted from his wife. Narad's pride is gone and his peace returns.
whole_arc_note: Do not stop at the monkey face as a joke. The whole arc: a real victory, pride in it, the warning ignored, the fall into the very thing he had conquered, rage at God, and a denial that was the kindness. Later Ram tells Narad he guards his devotees as a mother keeps a child from fire and snake.
teaching: The Lord's vow is the good of his servant, and that sometimes means refusing what the servant begs for.
framework: After a win, notice the story you tell about it. Heed the friend who says do not boast of this. When a strong wanting follows quickly, suspect the pride underneath. When refused, ask what the refusal protected.
modern_parallels: I finally got my habits under control and started lecturing everyone, then relapsed badly.
I prayed hard for that job and did not get it and I was furious at God.
After my promotion I stopped listening to the one person who warned me.
I wanted her so much I made a fool of myself in front of everyone.

key_verses.sanskrit: बार बार बिनवउँ मुनि तोही। जिमि यह कथा सुनायहु मोही॥ तिमि जनि हरिहि सुनावहु कबहूँ। चलेहुँ प्रसंग दुराएहु तबहूँ ॥
key_verses.gist: Shiva said: again and again I beg you, sage, never tell Hari this tale as you have told me; even if the subject arises, hide it.

key_verses.sanskrit: नारद कहेउ सहित अभिमाना। कृपा तुम्हारि सकल भगवाना॥ करुनानिधि मन दीख बिचारी। उर अंकुरेउ गरब तरु भारी ॥
key_verses.gist: The Lord of compassion considered: a great tree of pride has sprouted in his heart.

key_verses.sanskrit: कुपथ माग रुज ब्याकुल रोगी। बैद न देइ सुनहु मुनि जोगी॥ एहि बिधि हित तुम्हार मैं ठयऊ। कहि अस अंतरहित प्रभु भयऊ ॥
key_verses.gist: When a sick man, tormented, asks for the wrong food, the physician does not give it. So have I resolved on your good.

key_verses.sanskrit: मृषा होउ मम श्राप कृपाला। मम इच्छा कह दीनदयाला॥ मैं दुर्बचन कहे बहुतेरे। कह मुनि पाप मिटिहिं किमि मेरे ॥
key_verses.gist: I spoke many harsh words; how will my sin be wiped out?

content_hook: He beat desire in a straight fight. Then he bragged about it.

title: Manu and Shatarupa realise late that a full life has left something out
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 134 to 144 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Manu has ruled long and well and kept every law. Old age has come while he was still at home, and detachment from pleasures has not come with it. He feels sharp pain that a whole life has gone by without devotion.
what_they_did: He hands the kingdom to his son, almost by force, and goes with his wife to Naimisha. They live on less and less for thousands of years, refusing the boons Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva come to offer, wanting only to see the Lord.
the_turn: When the Lord appears and says ask, Manu hesitates and then speaks without pretence: I want a son like you; what is there to hide from the Lord. Shatarupa asks for the love and discernment of his own devotees.
outcome: They are promised that he himself will be born as their son. They become Dasharath and Kaushalya.
whole_arc_note: A devotional story of a couple acting together in the fourth stage of life. It does not tell a person with dependents to walk out; Manu settles the succession first. And the boon is asked honestly, with the heart's real wish.
teaching: It is not too late to turn; and before God one may ask for exactly what one wants.
modern_parallels: I have done everything right for forty years and something is still missing.
I retired last year and do not know what the rest of my life is for.
My husband and I want to give our remaining years to something that matters.
I am embarrassed by what I actually want to pray for.

key_verses.sanskrit: होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन॥ हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु ॥
key_verses.gist: Detachment from pleasures did not come, and living at home the fourth stage of life arrived; his heart ached that his life had passed without devotion to Hari.

key_verses.sanskrit: दानि सिरोमनि कृपानिधि नाथ कहउँ सतिभाउ। चाहउँ तुम्हहि समान सुत प्रभु सन कवन दुराउ ॥
key_verses.gist: Crown of givers, treasury of grace, I speak my true feeling: I want a son like you. What is there to hide from the Lord?

content_hook: He had been a good king his whole life. In old age it hurt that this was all he had been.

title: Pratapbhanu trusts a flatterer who promises he can have it all
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 144 to 165 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: A just and victorious king loses his way hunting and is taken in at a hermitage. The hermit is a king he once defeated, now in disguise. He speaks sweetly, hints at great powers, and asks what the king desires.
what_they_did: Pratapbhanu asks for a body free of age and death, to be unbeaten in war, and to rule the whole earth alone for a hundred ages. The hermit says only a brahmin's curse can stop this and offers to arrange a feast to win them over. Flesh is served by trickery, a voice from the sky exposes it, and the brahmins curse the king and his line to be born as demons.
the_turn: Tulsidas stops the story to say it: as the destiny is, so is the help that comes; either it comes to the man or it carries him to it. The king had everything and wanted it without limit or rival, and that wanting chose his adviser for him.
outcome: His kingdom falls to his enemies. He is reborn as Ravana.
whole_arc_note: He was a good king, which is the warning. The curse falls on a deception he did not intend; the text locates the fault earlier, in the boon he asked for and the secrecy he agreed to. Do not flatten it to a tale about bad luck.
teaching: Ambition without a limit makes a man easy for the flatterer who tells him there is a shortcut.
modern_parallels: A consultant promised us ten times growth if we kept the plan quiet from the board.
I trusted the one adviser who told me exactly what I wanted to hear.
I had a good business and bet it all on becoming the only player.
He was so humble and spiritual that I never checked who he was.

key_verses.sanskrit: जरा मरन दुख रहित तनु समर जितै जनि कोउ। एकछत्र रिपुहीन महि राज कलप सत होउ ॥
key_verses.gist: Let my body be free of age, death and pain, let none defeat me in battle, and let me rule the earth under one canopy, without a foe, for a hundred ages.

key_verses.sanskrit: तुलसी जसि भवतब्यता तैसी मिलइ सहाइ। आपुनु आवइ ताहि पहिं ताहि तहाँ लै जाइ ॥
key_verses.gist: Says Tulsi: as the fate to come, so the help one meets; either it comes to him, or it takes him there.

content_hook: Ravana was once a good king who asked one question too many: can I have all of it, for ever?
notes: The episode turns on a curse by brahmins; the telling here keeps to ambition and the false counsellor, which is how Tulsi frames it in 1.150.

title: The gods argue about where to go to find God
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 173 to 174 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The earth is crushed under Ravana's rule and the gods gather, frightened. They want to appeal to Hari and cannot agree where he is. One says go to Vaikuntha, another says the ocean of milk.
what_they_did: Shiva, sitting among them, speaks up. Brahma is moved to tears and they pray where they stand.
the_turn: Shiva's words: Hari is present everywhere alike; he becomes manifest through love, this I know. Tell me the place, time or direction where the Lord is not. He appears as fire appears from wood.
outcome: A voice answers from the sky promising the descent. They did not have to travel anywhere.
whole_arc_note: A devotional claim, not a dismissal of temples or pilgrimage. Its point is that love is the means by which the present becomes evident.
teaching: God is everywhere equally and shows himself where there is love.
modern_parallels: I moved abroad and there is no temple within two hours.
I do not know where to begin looking for God.
I am too unwell to go on the pilgrimage I promised.
I feel I am doing it wrong because I do not know the proper place or method.

key_verses.sanskrit: हरि ब्यापक सर्बत्र समाना। प्रेम तें प्रगट होहिं मैं जाना॥ देस काल दिसि बिदिसिहु माहीं। कहहु सो कहाँ जहाँ प्रभु नाहीं ॥
key_verses.gist: Hari pervades everywhere alike; he is revealed through love, this I know. Tell me the place, time or quarter where the Lord is not.

key_verses.sanskrit: अग जगमय सब रहित बिरागी। प्रेम तें प्रभु प्रगटइ जिमि आगी॥ मोर बचन सब के मन माना। साधु-साधु करि ब्रह्म बखाना ॥
key_verses.gist: Present in all that moves and does not move, apart from all and unattached, he appears through love as fire does.

content_hook: The gods could not agree on God's address. Shiva settled it in one line.

title: Kaushalya is overwhelmed by the child she is raising
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 189 to 190 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: She puts her baby down to sleep and goes to make the offering in the shrine. She finds him there eating it. She runs back and he is asleep in the cradle. Her mind reels: have I lost my wits, or is this something else?
what_they_did: The child smiles and shows her his whole form, with worlds beyond counting in every pore. She trembles, cannot speak, closes her eyes and bows. He becomes a baby again.
the_turn: She does not ask to see more. She folds her hands and asks that his maya never overtake her again. She wants to go on being his mother.
outcome: He tells her not to speak of it. Ordinary days of feeding and chasing a child resume.
whole_arc_note: A devotional vignette. Its human note is small and true: a parent glimpses that the child is far more than hers, and chooses the daily love over the vision.
teaching: Awe passes; what the mother asks to keep is the simple relationship.
modern_parallels: Some days I look at my baby and feel I have no idea who this person is.
I am overwhelmed as a new mother and scared I am getting it wrong.
My child is so unlike me that it frightens me.

key_verses.sanskrit: इहाँ उहाँ दुइ बालक देखा। मतिभ्रम मोर कि आन बिसेषा॥ देखि राम जननी अकुलानी। प्रभु हँसि दीन्ह मधुर मुसुकानी ॥
key_verses.gist: Here and there she saw two children: is my mind deceived, or is it something else? Seeing his mother distressed, the Lord gave a sweet smile.

key_verses.sanskrit: बार बार कौसल्या बिनय करइ कर जोरि। अब जनि कबहूँ ब्यापै प्रभु मोहि माया तोरि ॥
key_verses.gist: Again and again Kaushalya begged with folded hands: Lord, may your maya never come over me again.

content_hook: She saw the universe in her baby and asked for one thing: let me just be his mother.

title: Dasharath is asked to send his young sons into danger
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 193 to 197 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: He had sons only in old age. A sage arrives and asks for the two eldest to guard his sacrifice against demons. Dasharath's heart shakes and the colour leaves his face.
dilemma: His word to a guest and sage, against a father's terror for boys he thinks too young.
what_they_did: He offers land, cattle, treasure, his own life in a moment. He says all his sons are dear as life and Ram he cannot give. Where are fierce demons, and where my tender boy?
the_turn: Vasishtha explains at length and the king's doubt dissolves. He calls the boys, embraces them, and tells the sage: you are their father now.
outcome: The journey he feared is the one on which the boys prove themselves, Ahalya is freed, and Ram meets Sita.
whole_arc_note: His refusal is not shamed; the sage is pleased by the love in it. He lets go on the strength of counsel he trusts, without pretending he is unafraid.
teaching: Holding a child back out of love can keep him from the very road that makes him.
modern_parallels: My son wants to join the army and I cannot say yes.
She got into a college abroad and I keep finding reasons she should not go.
I had my child late and I know I am over-protective.
His coach says he is ready. I am not.

key_verses.sanskrit: सुनि राजा अति अप्रिय बानी। हृदय कंप मुख दुति कुमुलानी॥ चौथेंपन पायउँ सुत चारी। बिप्र बचन नहिं कहेहु बिचारी ॥
key_verses.gist: Hearing the unwelcome words his heart trembled and his face lost its light: in my fourth age I was given four sons; sage, you have not weighed what you ask.

key_verses.sanskrit: सब सुत प्रिय मोहि प्रान की नाईं। राम देत नहिं बनइ गोसाईं॥ कहँ निसिचर अति घोर कठोरा। कहँ सुंदर सुत परम किसोरा ॥
key_verses.gist: All my sons are dear to me as life; Ram I cannot give, master. Where are those fierce demons, and where my lovely young son?

content_hook: Take my kingdom, he said. Take my life. Not the boy.

title: Ahalya, after a long frozen wait, speaks without bitterness
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 198 to 199 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: She has been stone in an empty hermitage, cut off by a curse, with no way to shorten the time. Ram comes by on the road and the sage asks him to touch the rock with the dust of his feet.
what_they_did: She stands before him with folded hands, too full to speak, and weeps. Then she praises him and asks for nothing except that her mind stay at his feet.
the_turn: She says the curse the sage gave was a great good and she counts it the highest favour, because through it she has seen Hari with her own eyes.
outcome: She returns to her husband's world, full of joy.
whole_arc_note: This is her own first-person reading after release, as a devotee. It must never be turned outward as advice that a wronged or shamed person should be grateful for what was done to them. Tulsi keeps the cause in the background and gives her the dignity of the last word.
teaching: Seen from the far side of grace, even the long hard stretch can be owned as the road that led here.
modern_parallels: I lost years to a mistake and to other people's judgement of it.
For a long time I felt like stone, just waiting for something to change.
Looking back, the worst period of my life is what turned me toward God.

key_verses.sanskrit: परसत पद पावन सोकनसावन प्रगट भई तपपुंज सही। देखत रघुनायक जन सुखदायक सनमुख होइ कर जोरि रही॥ अति प्रेम अधीरा पुलक शरीरा मुख नहिं आवइ बचन कही। अतिसय बड़भागी चरनन्हि लागी जुगल नयन जलधार बही ॥
key_verses.gist: At the touch of the holy feet that end sorrow she stood revealed, radiant with austerity; overcome with love, no word would come, and tears streamed from her eyes.

key_verses.sanskrit: मुनि श्राप जो दीन्हा अति भल कीन्हा परम अनुग्रह मैं माना। देखेउँ भरि लोचन हरि भव मोचन इहइ लाभ संकर जाना॥ बिनती प्रभु मोरी मैं मति भोरी नाथ न मागउँ बर आना। पद कमल परागा रस अनुरागा मम मन मधुप करै पाना ॥
key_verses.gist: The curse the sage gave did me great good; I count it the highest favour, for I have seen Hari with my own eyes.

content_hook: She waited as stone for an age. Her first words were thanks.
notes: gender_sensitive: a woman cursed for an act in which she was deceived. Not for wronged stance. Use only as a devotee's retrospective voice.

title: Janak, the detached king, finds his heart pulled
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 203 to 204 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Janak is known as the king who lives in the world untouched by it. He comes to greet a visiting sage, sees two boys beside him, and something in him gives way.
what_they_did: He does not hide it or explain it away. He asks the sage in plain sincerity who they are.
the_turn: His own report: my mind is detachment itself by nature, and it is held still like the chakor before the moon; looking at them, it has dropped the joy of Brahman by force.
outcome: The sage smiles and says: you have spoken well; your word cannot be false.
whole_arc_note: The text treats this as the completion of his knowledge. Love for the Lord is shown as more compelling than impersonal peace.
teaching: Detachment is not the last word; love can still surprise the one who thought he was done.
modern_parallels: I worked hard to need nothing and nobody, and now I feel a pull I did not plan for.
I thought I had outgrown devotion. Then one visit to the temple undid me.
Nothing has moved me in years, and my grandchild has.

key_verses.sanskrit: सहज बिरागरूप मनु मोरा। थकित होत जिमि चंद चकोरा॥ ताते प्रभु पूछउँ सतिभाऊ। कहहु नाथ जनि करहु दुराऊ ॥
key_verses.gist: My mind is by nature dispassion itself, yet it stands entranced as the chakor before the moon; so I ask you in all sincerity, master, do not conceal it.

key_verses.sanskrit: इन्हहि बिलोकत अति अनुरागा। बरबस ब्रह्मसुखहि मन त्यागा॥ कह मुनि बिहसि कहेहु नृप नीका। बचन तुम्हार न होइ अलीका ॥
key_verses.gist: Looking at these two, great love arises; my mind has forcibly given up the bliss of Brahman.

content_hook: The most detached man in the kingdom looked up and lost his composure.

title: Ram notices his heart is stirred and says so to his brother
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 214 to 222 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Gathering flowers for his teacher in Janak's garden, Ram hears anklets, looks up and sees Sita. He cannot look away. He is a guest, she is unmarried, and nothing has been settled.
dilemma: A feeling he did not choose, in a place where he has no claim.
what_they_did: He turns to Lakshman and says it aloud: this is Janak's daughter, and at her unearthly beauty my naturally pure mind is disturbed. Then he reasons about it, goes back to the teacher and tells him everything.
the_turn: He trusts his own mind's record: the Raghus do not set foot on a wrong path, and I have full faith in this mind, which has never looked at another's wife even in dream. So the stirring itself must mean something; providence knows the cause.
outcome: The attraction is neither acted on in secret nor suppressed in shame. It is spoken, examined, reported to the guru, and fulfilled openly at the bow.
whole_arc_note: Tulsi's scene is love inside maryada. Clip it to love at first sight and the self-examination is lost; clip it to restraint and the frank admission is lost.
teaching: A mind that has kept itself clean can trust its own stirring, and the right way to carry a new feeling is in the open.
framework: Notice the feeling. Say it to someone you trust. Check it against your own record. Tell your elder or teacher. Let it be settled in the open.
modern_parallels: I have feelings for someone and I do not know if it is right to.
I am drawn to a colleague and keep pretending to myself that I am not.
I am scared to tell my family I like someone.
I do not trust my own judgement in love after last time.

key_verses.sanskrit: जासु बिलोकि अलौकिक सोभा। सहज पुनीत मोर मनु छोभा॥ सो सबु कारन जान बिधाता। फरकहिं सुभद अंग सुनु भ्राता ॥
key_verses.gist: At whose unearthly beauty my naturally pure mind is stirred; the cause of it all providence knows.

key_verses.sanskrit: रघुबंसिन्ह कर सहज सुभाऊ। मनु कुपंथ पगु धरइ न काऊ॥ मोहि अतिसय प्रतीति मन केरी। जेहिं सपनेहुँ परनारि न हेरी ॥
key_verses.gist: It is the nature of the Raghus that the mind never sets foot on a wrong path; I have full trust in my mind, which has not looked on another's wife even in dream.

content_hook: Ram fell in love in a garden and the first thing he did was tell his brother.

title: Sita wants something she is not free to ask for
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 222 to 224 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: She has seen Ram and her heart is settled on him. But her father has vowed she will marry whoever strings Shiva's bow, and that is not in her hands. She goes back into the temple.
what_they_did: She praises the goddess and then does not name the wish. She says: you know my heart's desire well, you live in the city of every heart, so I have not said it aloud; and she clasps the goddess's feet.
the_turn: The garland slips, the image smiles, and Gauri answers: the one your heart is set on, that dark and lovely groom, you shall have; he knows your goodness and your love.
outcome: She returns home glad, with nothing yet changed outwardly.
whole_arc_note: A prayer scene. The blessing comes before the outcome, and she still has to sit through the contest. Do not present it as wish fulfilment on demand.
teaching: What cannot be said to anyone can be laid before the one who already knows the heart.
modern_parallels: I know who I want to marry and the decision is not mine.
There is one thing I want so much I cannot even say it in prayer.
My result depends on a test I cannot influence.
I am waiting for my parents to agree.

key_verses.sanskrit: मोर मनोरथु जानहु नीकें। बसहु सदा उर पुर सबही कें॥ कीन्हेउँ प्रगट न कारन तेहीं। अस कहि चरन गहे बैदेहीं ॥
key_verses.gist: You know my heart's wish well, for you dwell in the city of every heart; that is why I have not spoken it. So saying, Vaidehi clasped her feet.

key_verses.sanskrit: मनु जाहिं राचेउ मिलिहि सो बरु सहज सुंदर साँवरो। करुना निधान सुजान सीलु सनेहु जानत रावरो॥ एहि भाँति गौरि असीस सुनि सिय सहित हियँ हरषीं अली। तुलसी भवानिहि पूजि पुनि पुनि मुदित मन मंदिर चली॥
key_verses.gist: The one on whom your heart is set, that naturally beautiful dark groom, you shall have; the compassionate and wise one knows your goodness and your love.

content_hook: She did not say the wish out loud. She said: you already know.

title: Sita watches the contest that will decide her life
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 243 to 246 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Ten thousand kings have failed to move the bow. Ram rises. She looks at him, tender and young, then remembers her father's vow, and her mind churns. She cannot help and she cannot look away.
what_they_did: Inwardly she cries out at her father's hard condition, begs the gods, and pleads with the bow itself to become light. She is embarrassed by her own agitation.
the_turn: She gathers herself and brings trust into her heart: if in body, mind and word my vow is true and my heart is given to his feet, then God who lives in every heart will make me his. Whoever truly loves someone will be united with them; of this there is no doubt.
outcome: Ram reads her state at a glance, lifts the bow, and it breaks.
whole_arc_note: Her frustration with her father is in the text and is not rebuked. The steadiness comes from her own truthfulness of love. She has no assurance of the result when she finds it.
teaching: Whoever holds a true love for another is certain to be joined to them.
modern_parallels: My whole future is being decided in a room I am not allowed to speak in.
I am sitting outside the interview hall for someone I love.
My father set a condition for my marriage that makes no sense to me.
All I can do now is wait for the result.

key_verses.sanskrit: नीकें निरखि नयन भरि सोभा। पितु पनु सुमिरि बहुरि मनु छोभा॥ अहह तात दारुनि हठ ठानी। समुझत नहिं कछु लाभु न हानी ॥
key_verses.gist: She looked her fill at his beauty, then remembered her father's vow and was troubled again: alas, father has taken a cruel stand and weighs neither gain nor loss.

key_verses.sanskrit: सकुची ब्याकुलता बड़ि जानी। धरि धींरजु प्रतीति उर आनी॥ तन मन बचन मोर पनु साचा। रघुपति पद सरोज चितु राचा ॥
key_verses.gist: Shy of her own great agitation, she took courage and brought trust into her heart: if my vow is true in body, mind and word, and my heart is given to Raghupati's feet,

key_verses.sanskrit: तौ भगवानु सकल उर बासी। करिहि मोहि रघुबर कै दासी॥ जेहि कें जेहि पर सत्य सनेहू। सो तेहि मिलइ न कछु संदेहू ॥
key_verses.gist: then God who dwells in every heart will make me his. Whoever truly loves another is united with them; of this there is no doubt.

content_hook: She could not lift the bow for him. She could only decide what to do with her fear.

title: Janak speaks in despair and Lakshman takes it as an insult
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 235 to 240 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Every king has failed. Janak, who staked his daughter's future on this test, loses heart in public: let no one boast of valour again; I see the earth is empty of heroes. Go home. Fate has not written a marriage for Vaidehi.
what_they_did: Lakshman, sitting beside Ram, bristles. His brows knit and his lips tremble. He says no one speaks so in a gathering where a Raghu is present, and offers to lift the whole universe like a ball.
the_turn: Ram checks his brother with a look, with affection, and seats him close. No rebuke, no counter-speech. Then the teacher says: rise, Ram, break the bow and end Janak's anguish.
outcome: The answer to the insult is the deed. Janak's despair turns to relief, like a tired swimmer touching bottom.
whole_arc_note: Three things together: a father's words spoken from pain and not meant as an attack, a young man's rightful sting at being written off, and an elder brother who neither shames the anger nor lets it run.
teaching: Words said in despair wound bystanders who were never the target; the reply that settles it is quiet action at the right moment.
modern_parallels: My boss said in the meeting that nobody on this team is capable, and I was sitting right there.
My father said in front of relatives that he has given up hope for his children.
I snapped back at a senior in public and now regret the tone, not the point.
I announced in frustration that the project was dead.

key_verses.sanskrit: अब जनि कोउ भाखे भट मानी। बीर बिहीन मही मैं जानी॥ तजहु आस निज निज गृह जाहू। लिखा न बिधि बैदेहि बिबाहू ॥
key_verses.gist: Let no one now boast of being a warrior; I see the earth is bare of heroes. Give up hope and go home; fate has not written a marriage for Vaidehi.

key_verses.sanskrit: रघुबंसिन्ह महुँ जहँ कोउ होई। तेहिं समाज अस कहइ न कोई॥ कही जनक जसि अनुचित बानी। बिद्यमान रघुकुल मनि जानी ॥
key_verses.gist: Where any of the Raghus is present, no one speaks such words in that assembly as Janak has spoken.

key_verses.sanskrit: गुर रघुपति सब मुनि मन माहीं। मुदित भए पुनि पुनि पुलकाहीं॥ सयनहिं रघुपति लखनु नेवारे। प्रेम समेत निकट बैठारे ॥
key_verses.gist: With a glance Raghupati checked Lakshman and, with love, seated him close.

content_hook: There are no heroes left, said the king, with two of them sitting in front of him.

title: Sunayana fears the boy is too slight for the task
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 241 to 243 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Sita's mother watches Ram walk toward the bow that defeated Ravana and Bana. She turns to her friends in distress: why does no one stop the teacher? This is a child. All our wisdom has come to nothing.
what_they_did: A clever companion answers her gently with examples.
the_turn: The companion says: do not count the radiant as small. The sun looks small and lights the three worlds. A mantra is tiny and commands the gods; a little goad governs a mad elephant.
outcome: The queen takes courage and her love for Ram grows. When the bow breaks she is like a parched field that has received rain.
whole_arc_note: Light and brief; it is consolation offered to a frightened mother by a friend, with reasons.
teaching: Do not judge the brilliant by their size.
modern_parallels: Everyone on the panel is twice my age and I can see them deciding I am too young.
My daughter is small for her age and I worry constantly before her matches.
We are a five-person company pitching against giants.

key_verses.sanskrit: भूप सयानप सकल सिरानी। सखि बिधि गति कछु जाति न जानी॥ बोली चतुर सखी मृदु बानी। तेजवंत लघु गनिअ न रानी ॥
key_verses.gist: A clever companion said softly: queen, the radiant are not to be reckoned small.

key_verses.sanskrit: मंत्र परम लघु जासु बस बिधि हरि हर सुर सर्ब। महामत्त गजराज कहुँ बस कर अंकुस खर्ब ॥
key_verses.gist: The mantra is very small, yet Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and all the gods are in its power; a little goad masters the great maddened elephant.

content_hook: He is only a boy, said the queen. Her friend pointed at the sun.

title: Parashuram storms in; Lakshman needles him and Ram disarms him
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 247 to 271 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The bow is broken, the garland given, and a furious elder walks into the celebration demanding to know who did it. He is famous, feared, and sure he has been insulted. The hall goes silent.
dilemma: Answer an older man's public rage with truth that stings, or with humility that might look like fear.
what_they_did: Ram answers first, softly: whoever broke Shiva's bow will be some servant of yours. Lakshman cannot resist: we broke many little bows as boys and you never minded; why so attached to this one? Each taunt raises the heat. Ram keeps stepping in, taking the blame on himself and asking pardon for a boy's mistake.
the_turn: Ram does not yield the fact, only the tone. He says our name is only Ram and yours has an axe attached; forgive what was done unknowingly. His steadiness lets Parashuram see who stands before him; he hands over Vishnu's bow, and it strings itself.
outcome: Parashuram folds his hands, praises both brothers, asks their pardon and leaves for the forest.
whole_arc_note: Both brothers are needed. Lakshman's wit says what everyone is thinking and nearly gets them killed; Ram's courtesy carries the same truth to a place the angry man can hear it. Ram also says, mildly, that even the crooked moon is spared by Rahu: straightforwardness can be a fault with some people.
teaching: A hot answer feeds anger; a calm one that gives no ground on the facts lets it burn out.
modern_parallels: A senior walked into my meeting and shouted at me in front of everyone.
My father-in-law lost his temper at our wedding function.
I am very good at the sarcastic reply and it always makes things worse.
How do I stay respectful to an elder who is being unreasonable without grovelling?

key_verses.sanskrit: नाथ संभुधनु भंजनिहारा। होइहि केउ एक दास तुम्हारा॥ आयसु काह कहिअ किन मोही। सुनि रिसाइ बोले मुनि कोही ॥
key_verses.gist: Lord, the one who broke Shambhu's bow will be some servant of yours. What is your command? Why not tell me?

key_verses.sanskrit: बहु धनुहीं तोरीं लरिकाईं। कबहुँ न असि रिस कीन्हि गोसाईं॥ एहि धनु पर ममता केहि हेतू। सुनि रिसाइ कह भृगुकुलकेतू ॥
key_verses.gist: We broke many small bows in childhood and you were never so angry, master. Why such attachment to this one?

key_verses.sanskrit: जौं तुम्ह औतेहु मुनि की नाईं। पद रज सिर सिसु धरत गोसाईं॥ छमहु चूक अनजानत केरी। चहिअ बिप्र उर कृपा घनेरी ॥
key_verses.gist: Forgive a fault done unknowingly; a brahmin's heart should hold abundant mercy.

key_verses.sanskrit: जाना राम प्रभाउ तब पुलक प्रफुल्लित गात। जोरि पानि बोले बचन हृदयँ न प्रेमु अमात ॥
key_verses.gist: Then he knew Ram's greatness; his body thrilled, and with folded hands he spoke, his heart unable to contain its love.

content_hook: One brother answered the angry man with jokes. The other answered with an apology he did not owe.

title: Janak, the knower of the Self, cannot let his daughter go
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand, dohas 313 to 322 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The wedding is over and the palanquins are ready. Janak is the king who is called Videha, beyond the body, a man of settled wisdom. He takes Sita in his arms and it all leaves him.
what_they_did: He holds her to his chest again and again. His ministers reason with him. He considers that this is no time for weeping, calls for the palanquin, seats her himself, and then walks a long way with the departing party.
the_turn: Tulsi says it outright: seeing Sita, his composure fled; he who was called supremely dispassionate; the great boundary of his wisdom was washed away. The text lets it be so. Then, parting from Ram, Janak asks for one thing: may my mind never leave your feet.
outcome: She goes. He returns to an emptied house and remains its king.
whole_arc_note: The poem does not correct his tears with philosophy. A wise man weeps, and then does what the hour requires. Both stand.
teaching: Wisdom does not cancel a father's love, and love does not excuse him from letting go.
modern_parallels: My daughter's wedding is next month and I cannot get through a day without crying.
I teach detachment to others and I fell apart when my son left for college.
The house is so quiet since she moved out.
I am supposed to be the strong one in the family.

key_verses.sanskrit: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥
key_verses.gist: Seeing Sita, his composure fled, he who was called supremely dispassionate; the king held Janaki to his heart, and the great boundary of his wisdom was effaced.

key_verses.sanskrit: समुझावत सब सचिव सयाने। कीन्ह बिचारु न अवसर जाने॥ बारहिं बार सुता उर लाईं। सजि सुंदर पालकीं मगाईं ॥
key_verses.gist: All his wise ministers reasoned with him; he judged it no time for grief, embraced his daughter again and again, and called for a fine palanquin.

key_verses.sanskrit: बार बार मागउँ कर जोरें। मनु परिहरै चरन जनि भोरें॥ सुनि बर बचन प्रेम जनु पोषे। पूरनकाम रामु परितोषे ॥
key_verses.gist: Again and again I beg with folded hands: may my mind never, even by mistake, leave your feet.

content_hook: They called him the king beyond the body. Then his daughter got into the palanquin.

title: Dasharath sees a white hair and decides to hand over
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 2 to 5 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The king sits in court at the height of his good fortune. By chance he takes a mirror to straighten his crown and sees that the hair by his ears has turned white.
what_they_did: He takes it as a message, goes to his teacher, and says he has one wish left: to see Ram made heir while he himself is alive.
the_turn: He reads the white hair as old age itself giving counsel: give Ram the regency and take the reward of having lived.
outcome: The preparation begins that night. What follows is not what he planned, but the decision itself is praised by all.
whole_arc_note: The handover is wise and still goes wrong for reasons outside it. Do not make the story promise that letting go on time guarantees a smooth result.
teaching: The body tells you when it is time to pass the work on; the wise act on the first sign.
modern_parallels: I am sixty-one and still cannot bring myself to name a successor.
I noticed in the mirror this morning that I look like my father did when he retired.
My children are ready to run the business. I am the one who is not.

key_verses.sanskrit: श्रवन समीप भए सित केसा। मनहुँ जरठपनु अस उपदेसा॥ नृप जुबराजु राम कहुँ देहू। जीवन जनम लाहु किन लेहू ॥
key_verses.gist: The hair beside his ears had turned white, as though old age were advising him: king, give Ram the regency and take the reward of your life and birth.

content_hook: One white hair in the mirror, and the king went to find his successor.

title: Ram hears he is to be crowned and is troubled for his brothers
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 8 to 12 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The teacher has come to say that tomorrow he will be made heir. The city is already celebrating. Ram, alone with the news, finds one thing in it that sits wrong.
what_they_did: He thinks back: we brothers were born together; we ate, slept and played together; ear-piercing, sacred thread, weddings, every celebration was shared. And now one is to be raised and three left out.
the_turn: His words to himself: in this spotless line this one thing is unfitting, that the eldest alone is anointed, apart from his brothers. Tulsi calls this loving regret beautiful and prays it may remove the crookedness from devotees' hearts.
outcome: Within a day the crown passes from him, and he takes that with the same evenness with which he took the offer.
whole_arc_note: It is the root of the later scene. A man who was uneasy at being preferred is not broken when he is passed over.
teaching: To feel the unfairness of your own advantage is a mark of love.
modern_parallels: I got the promotion and my closest friend on the team did not.
My parents are leaving the house to me and nothing to my sister.
I feel guilty being the favourite.
I was picked as lead over people who started with me.

key_verses.sanskrit: जनमे एक संग सब भाई। भोजन सयन केलि लरिकाई॥ करनबेध उपबीत बिआहा। संग संग सब भए उछाहा ॥
key_verses.gist: We brothers were all born together; eating, sleeping and childhood play, ear-piercing, sacred thread and marriage, every joy came to us together.

key_verses.sanskrit: बिमल बंस यहु अनुचित एकू। बंधु बिहाइ बड़ेहि अभिषेकू॥ प्रभु सप्रेम पछितानि सुहाई। हरउ भगत मन कै कुटिलाई ॥
key_verses.gist: In this spotless line this one thing is unfitting, that the eldest alone should be anointed, apart from his brothers.

content_hook: The night before his coronation, Ram's one worry was that it was not fair to his brothers.

title: Kaikeyi, who loved Ram, is talked into fearing him
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 13 to 26 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Kaikeyi hears of the coronation and is delighted. She says all the mothers are as dear to Ram as Kaushalya and he loves her most of all; she has tested it. Her maid sits sulking and will not say why.
what_they_did: She scolds the maid and threatens to have her tongue pulled out. Then she asks again, on Bharat's oath, what the matter is. Manthara plays reluctant: whoever is king, what is it to me; will I stop being a servant? Bit by bit she draws a picture of Kaushalya ruling, Bharat jailed, Kaikeyi a fly picked out of milk.
the_turn: The turning is small: Kaikeyi asks to hear more. Manthara never argues that Ram is bad. She plants a future in which Kaikeyi is humiliated, and fear does the rest. Tulsi's comment: who is not ruined by bad company; in a low counsel cleverness does not survive.
outcome: The woman who loved Ram demands his exile, loses her husband, and is disowned by the son she did it for.
whole_arc_note: Tulsi adds that the gods moved Sarasvati to twist Manthara's mind, and never makes Kaikeyi a simple villain. Her remorse at Chitrakoot and Ram greeting her first belong to the same story. The lesson concerns a voice one keeps listening to and does not concern women or stepmothers.
teaching: A settled, loving mind can be turned by one insinuating voice if it keeps listening.
framework: Notice who gains by your alarm. Notice when someone says they have nothing to gain. Check the picture against your own long experience of the person. Do not decide in the sulking-room.
modern_parallels: A relative keeps telling me my brother will cheat me out of the property.
One colleague has convinced me the new manager is out to get me.
I was happy for her until someone pointed out what her success means for me.
I read one thread online and now I cannot trust my own husband.

key_verses.sanskrit: कौसल्या सम सब महतारी। रामहि सहज सुभायँ पिआरी॥ मो पर करहिं सनेहु बिसेषी। मैं करि प्रीति परीछा देखी ॥
key_verses.gist: To Ram all the mothers are as dear as Kaushalya by nature, and he shows me special love; I have tested his affection.

key_verses.sanskrit: करि कुरूप बिधि परबस कीन्हा। बवा सो लुनिअ लहिअ जो दीन्हा॥ कोउ नृप होउ हमहि का हानी। चेरि छाड़ि अब होब कि रानी ॥
key_verses.gist: Whoever is king, what do I lose? Shall I cease to be a maid and become a queen?

key_verses.sanskrit: अस अभिलाषु नगर सब काहू। कैकयसुता हृदयँ अति दाहू॥ को न कुसंगति पाइ नसाई। रहइ न नीच मतें चतुराई ॥
key_verses.gist: Who is not ruined by bad company? In a low mind's counsel no cleverness remains.

content_hook: At breakfast she loved Ram like her own son. By evening she wanted him gone. One conversation did it.
notes: gender_sensitive: the passage contains generalisations about women spoken in the scene; none are used here.

title: Dasharath is held to a promise that will destroy what he loves
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 26 to 40 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: He comes to his favourite queen in good spirits and finds her on the floor of the sulking-room. To coax her he swears by Ram that she may have anything. She asks for two things: Bharat crowned, Ram in the forest fourteen years.
dilemma: Break his sworn word, or keep it and exile his blameless son.
what_they_did: He pleads through the night, offers Bharat the throne gladly, begs only that Ram may stay. He falls at her feet. He cannot bring himself to say go and cannot say stay.
the_turn: The line he himself had spoken a moment earlier becomes the trap: it has ever been the way of the Raghus that life may go but the word does not. He had promised blind, in a moment of fondness, with an oath he could not take back.
outcome: Ram resolves it for him by going. The king dies of the separation within days.
whole_arc_note: The text honours his truthfulness and shows its price. It does not say he should have broken his word, and it does not hide that the promise was made carelessly. Both are true.
teaching: Life may go, but the given word may not; so be careful what you give it to.
modern_parallels: I gave my word years ago and keeping it now will hurt someone I love.
I signed something in a good mood and I am trapped by it.
My wife is asking me to choose between her and my son from my first marriage.
I promised a co-founder terms that are now ruining the company.

key_verses.sanskrit: झूठेहुँ हमहि दोषु जनि देहू। दुइ कै चारि मागि मकु लेहू॥ रघुकुल रीति सदा चलि आई। प्रान जाहुँ परु बचनु न जाई ॥
key_verses.gist: It has ever been the way of Raghu's line: let life go, but not the given word.

content_hook: He swore by his son's name to give her anything. She asked for his son.

title: Ram is told he has lost the throne and must leave by morning
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 40 to 50 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: He is summoned on what should be his coronation morning. His father lies speechless on the floor. Kaikeyi, sitting unafraid, tells him the whole of it in hard words, like a figure of harshness itself.
what_they_did: He smiles inwardly and answers gently, with no fault in his words: fortunate is the son who loves his parents' word. In the forest I shall meet the sages, which is in every way my good; there is father's command in it, and your wish. Then he worries only that his father is suffering over so small a thing.
the_turn: Tulsi's image: Ram's mind was a young elephant and kingship its chain; hearing he was freed to go to the forest, the joy in his heart grew.
outcome: He comforts his father, takes leave, and goes to tell his mother.
whole_arc_note: This is Ram's own nature and choice. It is not a rule that someone cheated out of what is theirs must smile. The text shows the city furious at the injustice, and does not blame them.
teaching: To one not bound to the prize, losing it can feel like release.
modern_parallels: The role I was promised went to someone else this morning.
I have been told to relocate and step down, effective immediately.
Strangely, I felt relief when the offer fell through.
How do I not become bitter about this?

key_verses.sanskrit: सुनु जननी सोइ सुतु बड़भागी। जो पितु मातु बचन अनुरागी॥ तनय मातु पितु तोषनिहारा। दुर्लभ जननि सकल संसारा ॥
key_verses.gist: Listen, mother: that son is fortunate who loves the word of his father and mother.

key_verses.sanskrit: मुनिगन मिलनु बिसेषि बन सबहि भाँति हित मोर। तेहि महँ पितु आयसु बहुरि संमत जननी तोर ॥
key_verses.gist: In the forest I shall meet the sages, which is my good in every way; in it too is father's command, and your consent, mother.

key_verses.sanskrit: नव गयंदु रघुबीर मनु राजु अलान समान। छूट जानि बन गवनु सुनि उर अनंदु अधिकान ॥
key_verses.gist: Raghubir's mind was a young elephant, kingship its fetter; hearing he was to go to the forest, he knew himself released and joy grew in his heart.

content_hook: He lost a kingdom before breakfast and Tulsidas compares him to an elephant slipping its chain.

title: Kaushalya can neither keep her son nor tell him to go
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 50 to 59 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Ram comes to her cheerful and says father has given him the kingdom of the forest. She understands slowly. She is the wronged wife and the mother of the wronged son, and he is asking for her blessing to leave.
dilemma: If she holds him back, dharma is lost and the brothers divided. If she says go, she loses him.
what_they_did: She stands caught, like the snake that has seized a musk-rat and can neither swallow nor let go. Then, taking great courage, she speaks.
the_turn: Her ruling is exact: if it is your father's order alone, do not go, for a mother is greater. If father and mother both have said it, then the forest is a hundred Ayodhyas to you.
outcome: She blesses him, asks only not to be forgotten, and later is the one who comforts Bharat.
whole_arc_note: She does not simply submit. She first asserts a mother's standing above the father's command, and then counts Kaikeyi as his mother too. Her grief is not removed; she acts through it.
teaching: Love that sees dharma clearly can bless the very thing that breaks its heart.
modern_parallels: My son has decided to take a posting I think is unjust, and he wants my blessing.
If I fight this, I split the family. If I do not, I lose my child.
I was passed over by my husband's family for years and now they have done it to my son.
How do I let her go without making her carry my grief?

key_verses.sanskrit: राखि न सकइ न कहि सक जाहू। दुहूँ भाँति उर दारुन दाहू॥ लिखत सुधाकर गा लिखि राहू। बिधि गति बाम सदा सब काहू ॥
key_verses.gist: She could not keep him and could not say go; either way a terrible burning in her heart.

key_verses.sanskrit: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥
key_verses.gist: Dharma and love both held her mind; she was like the snake with the musk-rat. If I keep my son, dharma goes and the brothers are set against each other.

key_verses.sanskrit: जौं केवल पितु आयसु ताता। तौ जनि जाहु जानि बड़ि माता॥ जौं पितु मातु कहेउ बन जाना। तौ कानन सत अवध समाना ॥
key_verses.gist: If it is your father's command alone, then do not go, knowing the mother greater. If father and mother both have said go, the forest is a hundred Ayodhyas.

content_hook: She did not say go. She did not say stay. What she said was more precise than either.

title: Sita refuses to be left behind in comfort
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 60 to 67 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Ram, in front of his mother, explains to Sita why she must stay: the forest has thorns, heat, wild animals, bark clothes. He is kind and thorough and has already decided for her.
dilemma: Accept a decision made lovingly on her behalf, or contest it.
what_they_did: She touches her mother-in-law's feet, asks pardon for speaking, and answers every point. Without you heaven is hell to me. Who would dare look at me beside you? And then, with an edge: I am delicate and you, lord, are fit for the forest? Austerity is right for you and comfort for me?
the_turn: She tells him plainly that if he leaves her in Ayodhya for the term, he should know her life will not last. He looks at her and understands that this is simply true, and gives up his plan.
outcome: She goes. Her presence in the forest is counted her own choice from the first step.
whole_arc_note: Her speech uses the idiom of a wife's devotion, and it is also an argument she wins against her husband and the elders. The scene shows a woman's own decision prevailing and should not be used to tell anyone to follow a spouse.
teaching: To one who loves, hardship shared is lighter than comfort apart; and that is for her to say.
modern_parallels: My husband wants me to stay with his parents while he takes the hardship posting alone.
Everyone is deciding what is best for me without asking.
I would rather struggle together than be safe apart.
He thinks he is protecting me by leaving me out of it.

key_verses.sanskrit: को प्रभु सँग मोहि चितवनिहारा। सिंघबधुहि जिमि ससक सिआरा॥ मैं सुकुमारि नाथ बन जोगू। तुम्हहि उचित तप मो कहुँ भोगू ॥
key_verses.gist: Who can so much as look at me when I am with my lord, any more than hare or jackal at a lioness? I am delicate and you fit for the forest? Austerity right for you and pleasure for me?

key_verses.sanskrit: राखिअ अवध जो अवधि लगि रहत न जनिअहिं प्रान। दीनबंधु सुंदर सुखद सील सनेह निधान ॥
key_verses.gist: If you keep me in Avadh for the term, know that my life will not stay.

content_hook: Ram listed every danger of the forest. Sita's reply: so I am the delicate one, and you are not?
notes: gender_sensitive: the pati-vrata idiom of the speech (2.64) is not used as a teaching line.

title: Sumitra tells her son to go, and means it
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 69 to 75 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: Lakshman has begged Ram to take him, saying he knows no teacher, father or mother but him. Ram sends him to ask his own mother. He goes afraid she will hold him back out of love.
what_they_did: She hears it and is stricken like a doe in a forest fire. Then, seeing the hour, she steadies herself and speaks as his well-wisher.
the_turn: Her words: Vaidehi is your mother now and Ram your father. Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives, as day is wherever the sun shines. If Sita and Ram are going to the forest, you have no business in Avadh.
outcome: Lakshman leaves at once, relieved, like a deer that has slipped a snare.
whole_arc_note: She has no share in the quarrel and gains nothing. Her firmness is spoken through grief, in an ill hour she recognises as such. Devotional in its reasoning; the human core is a mother who removes herself as her son's excuse.
teaching: Home is where the one you serve is; a mother's love can be the thing that frees a son to go.
modern_parallels: My son wants to move across the country to care for his brother and is waiting for me to object.
I do not want to be the reason my daughter turns down what she believes in.
My mother told me to go. I still feel guilty.
I am the parent who stays behind and is never mentioned.

key_verses.sanskrit: मैं सिसु प्रभु सनेहँ प्रतिपाला। मंदरु मेरु कि लेहिं मराला॥ गुर पितु मातु न जानउँ काहू। कहउँ सुभाउ नाथ पतिआहू ॥
key_verses.gist: I am a child reared on my lord's love. I know no teacher, father or mother; I speak my nature, believe me.

key_verses.sanskrit: धीरजु धरेउ कुअवसर जानी। सहज सुहृद बोली मृदु बानी॥ तात तुम्हारि मातु बैदेही। पिता रामु सब भाँति सनेही ॥
key_verses.gist: Seeing the hour was ill she took courage and spoke gently: son, Vaidehi is your mother and Ram, in every way loving, your father.

key_verses.sanskrit: अवध तहाँ जहँ राम निवासू। तहँइँ दिवसु जहँ भानु प्रकासू॥ जौं पै सीय रामु बन जाहीं। अवध तुम्हार काजु कछु नाहीं ॥
key_verses.gist: Avadh is where Ram dwells, as day is where the sun shines. If Sita and Ram go to the forest, you have nothing to do in Avadh.

content_hook: He came to ask permission, braced for tears. His mother said: why are you still here?

title: Ram slips away at night from people who will not let him go
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 77 to 85 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The whole city has followed him to the riverbank, old and young, saying where Ram is there is Ayodhya. He reasons with them tenderly and they will not turn back. They fall asleep, worn out with grief.
dilemma: Stay and be held by their love, or leave without their consent.
what_they_did: He is torn; love and courtesy are hard to set aside. After midnight he asks the charioteer to drive so that the tracks cannot be followed.
the_turn: His words to Sumantra: drive the chariot and confuse the trail, friend; there is no other way this can be done.
outcome: They wake to find him gone, blame their own sleep, and return to wait out fourteen years.
whole_arc_note: It is the only quiet deception Ram practises on those who love him, and the text presents it as the kindest option available. It does not license disappearing on people in general.
teaching: Sometimes those who love you cannot release you, and you must go without the goodbye they want.
modern_parallels: My parents cry every time I leave, so I have started booking early morning flights.
My team begged me not to resign and I do not know how to walk out.
I left without a proper goodbye because I knew I would not be able to leave otherwise.

key_verses.sanskrit: सीलु सनेहु छाड़ि नहिं जाई। असमंजस बस भे रघुराई॥ लोग सोग श्रम बस गए सोई। कछुक देवमायाँ मति मोई ॥
key_verses.gist: Love and courtesy could not be set aside; Raghurai was caught in a dilemma. The people slept, overcome by grief and weariness.

key_verses.sanskrit: जबहिं जाम जुग जामिनि बीती। राम सचिव सन कहेउ सप्रीती॥ खोज मारि रथु हाँकहु ताता। आन उपायँ बनिहि नहिं बाता ॥
key_verses.gist: When two watches of the night had passed, Ram said lovingly to the minister: drive the chariot so as to hide the tracks, friend; in no other way will this be managed.

content_hook: A whole city followed him out of town. He waited until they fell asleep.

title: Guha rages at Kaikeyi; Lakshman tells him no one gives another joy or sorrow
source_ref: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, dohas 86 to 94 (corpus and library numbering; Gita Press counts run a few dohas higher)
the_moment: The tribal chief Guha keeps watch through the night and sees Ram and Sita asleep on a bed of grass and leaves. He thinks of the palace beds and weeps, and his grief turns to anger at the queen who caused it.
what_they_did: Lakshman, awake beside him with his bow, answers in sweet and gentle words steeped in knowledge, dispassion and devotion.
the_turn: No one is the giver of joy or sorrow to another; each meets the fruit of his own acts, brother. As a king dreams himself a beggar, or a pauper lord of heaven, and on waking has neither gained nor lost, so see this world. Thinking so, do not be angry, and do not blame anyone in vain.
outcome: The night passes in talk of Ram. In the morning Guha serves them and helps them cross.
whole_arc_note: This is said by the injured party, about his own family's misfortune, to a friend whose anger is on their behalf. It is not said to a victim about their abuser. Lakshman himself explodes later when he thinks Bharat is coming to attack; the text keeps both.
teaching: No one else is the giver of your joy or sorrow.
modern_parallels: I cannot stop being angry at the person who did this to my friend.
My brother got pushed out of the family business and he is calmer about it than I am.
I lie awake listing who is to blame.
Seeing someone I admire reduced to this breaks me.

key_verses.sanskrit: बोले लखन मधुर मृदु बानी। ग्यान बिराग भगति रस सानी॥ काहु न कोउ सुख दुख कर दाता। निज कृत करम भोग सबु भ्राता ॥
key_verses.gist: No one is the giver of joy or sorrow to another; all experience the fruit of their own deeds, brother.
